title: Geometric reducedness over a perfect field
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over a perfect field
$K$, where perfect means that $K$ has characteristic $0$, or has
characteristic $p>0$ and the map $a\mapsto a^p$ is surjective on $K$.
For every field extension $L/K$, the scheme $X_L$ is
reduced. Consequently $X\to\Spec(K)$ is flat and of finite
presentation and has geometrically reduced fibres.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the structure morphism. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $K$-algebra. Each $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is reduced by the section-wise characterization in [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The empty cover is allowed when $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01J1, lemma-reduced; finite affine cover as in the blueprint proof opening and the finite-type definition

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field extension $L/K$. A field is reduced: if $b^n=0$ and $b\ne0$, multiplication by $(b^{-1})^n$ gives $1=0$. Thus both $A_i$ and $L$ are reduced $K$-algebras. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] with $k=K$, $R=A_i$, $S=L$ to obtain that $A_i\otimes_K L$ is reduced for every $i$. This application needs neither that $L/K$ be algebraic nor that $L$ be finitely generated.

Let $p:X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ be the first projection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with base open $\operatorname{Spec}K$, source open $U_i$, and second-factor open $\operatorname{Spec}L$. It identifies $p^{-1}(U_i)$ with $U_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L$ as an open subscheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_K L)$, which is reduced by step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. Reducedness is invariant under these isomorphisms because their induced isomorphisms on local rings take nilpotent elements to nilpotent elements in both directions. The inverse images $p^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $X_L$ because the $U_i$ cover $X$.

For any open $V\subseteq X_L$ and nilpotent section $s\in\mathcal O_{X_L}(V)$, its restriction to each $V\cap p^{-1}(U_i)$ is nilpotent and therefore zero, since the open subschemes in step 3 are reduced. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom gives $s=0$. The section-wise criterion in [def-pc-reduced-scheme] now proves $X_L$ reduced. Since $L/K$ was arbitrary, this is geometric reducedness in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] (its reducedness clause). By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has a single point $y$ with residue field $K$. The only prime ideal of $K$ is $(0)$, and localization at its complement inverts elements already invertible in $K$. Thus the local ring and residue field are canonically $K$, their quotient map is the identity under these identifications, and the canonical residue-field morphism is identified with the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $X_y=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}K$ along this identity. Let $a:X_y\to X$ and $b:X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be its projections. By [def-pc-fibre-product], the pair $(\mathrm{id}_X,f)$ induces $j:X\to X_y$ with $a\circ j=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $b\circ j=f$. Since $b=f\circ a$, the composites $j\circ a$ and $\mathrm{id}_{X_y}$ have equal composites with both projections and are equal by uniqueness. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism over $K$. Its base change to any $L/K$ is also an isomorphism: apply fibre-product functoriality to $a,j$; their composites are identities by the same uniqueness. Consequently $(X_y)_L\cong X_L$ is reduced for every $L/K$, so $f$ has geometrically reduced fibres.

source.place: Tag 01J1, lemma-reduced, sheaf-local argument; geometric reducedness over the single-point base

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-flat-field] to the $K$-scheme $X$. It states that every morphism of a scheme to the spectrum of a field is flat, so $f$ is flat, with no reducedness or finiteness hypothesis needed for this step.

source.place: Flat instance for a subsingleton integral target, lines 115-121 (field case)

proof.text: The field $K$ is Noetherian, since an ideal containing a nonzero element contains its inverse multiple $1$, so the only ideals are $(0)$ and $K$. For each chart from step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes the finitely generated $K$-algebra $A_i$ finitely presented over $K$. These affine neighbourhoods of every point are exactly the local condition of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation, assertion (3); affine local definition of finite presentation

proof.text: The one affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and the ideal argument in step 6, and its one-point space is quasi-compact. Therefore it is Noetherian in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply that node to the finite-type morphism $f$ to obtain that $X$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is quasi-separated. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] then makes $f$ quasi-separated. This argument does not assume that $f$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Properties Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated; source-quasi-separated permanence

proof.text: The finite-type hypothesis already includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Together with local finite presentation from step 6 and quasi-separatedness from step 7, this proves that $f$ is of finite presentation by the finite-presentation convention in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Combining this with steps 4 and 5 gives all clauses of the statement.
